files.why: 'Finance may void' is a business rule about invoices, so canVoid gains the actor's roles and requires the finance role alongside the existing status check (stays framework-free).
canVoidInvoice must fold in the current user's roles: read them from the shared session reader and pass them to canVoid so the computed drives the button's visibility.
Existing canVoid tests assert status-only behavior and will break; extend them to cover the finance-role requirement (finance-with-unpaid = true, non-finance = false).

No auth concept exists anywhere; a pure Role vocabulary including 'finance' must live in shared/lib because billing/core is only allowed to import shared/lib (per the allow-list) and roles are cross-cutting, not a billing domain noun.
The UI needs a reactive reader of the signed-in user's roles; shared/lib is importable by slice ui/ and holds framework composables already (useDebounce), and 'user/role' is not a banned domain noun.
Someone must seed the current user/roles at startup; the composition root owns providers (app-is-a-leaf means slices can't read app, so it only writes into the shared session reader).
Bootstrap must initialize the session provider before mount, next to startMockApi(), so roles are available when views render.

uncertain: Biggest one: WHERE identity/roles should live. There is no auth infrastructure anywhere in the repo. I placed it in shared/lib + an app provider because that needs no architecture-review changes, but the more constitution-faithful home is a NEW 'access'/'identity' slice (core=Role+hasRole rule, data=current-user query/mock/store, ui=useCurrentUser, empty routes.ts, index.ts) consumed by billing via @slices/access — the canonical cross-slice pattern. That path is heavier: it edits the CODEOWNERS-protected `slices` list in architecture.config.ts and thus requires architecture review.

Whether the void rule belongs in billing/core (canVoid(invoice, roles)) or should stay status-only in core with the role check done in the ui composable. I chose core because 'finance may void' is a business rule, but it makes core reference a role vocabulary.

Global reactive state has no sanctioned home: 'stores' is a banned directory and Pinia stores are meant to live in a slice's data/. So I used a shared/lib singleton composable rather than a store, which may be considered a smell.
InvoiceDetailView.vue intentionally needs NO change — its Button is already v-if="canVoidInvoice", so hiding falls out of the composable. Flagging in case reviewers expected a view edit.

If roles are fetched (not seeded synchronously), a current-user MSW mock is needed, but mock handlers are composed per-slice from data/mocks.ts in app/providers/msw.ts — a session mock has no slice to belong to, reinforcing the identity-home question.
questions: There is no existing auth/user/role/session concept in the codebase at all — is one being introduced elsewhere (backend, another PR), or am I standing up the first identity mechanism here? This determines almost every placement above.

Should identity be a new slice (needs architecture review to add to architecture.config.ts + CODEOWNERS) or shared primitives? Feature work is explicitly not supposed to touch architecture files, so I need a ruling.
Where does the current user's role actually come from at runtime — a /api/me endpoint (needs a mock + query), a JWT/claims, or injected config? That decides data/ vs synchronous app seed.
Should the void mutation endpoint also enforce finance-only server-side (defense in depth), or is hiding the button sufficient for this request? The ask only mentions the button.
Exact role model: is it a single role or a set of roles per user, and is 'finance' the canonical string? Also, do admins/superusers implicitly get void rights?
